Chapter 7: Discovering Your Own ‘Why’—A Personal Journey
You know, while organizations really come alive with a shared sense of purpose, the same is true for each of us as individuals. When you tap into your own ‘why’, life just feels a little more meaningful, a little more energized.
Discovering your personal purpose isn’t about inventing some grand mission statement, or trying to follow someone else’s footsteps. It’s about looking inward—reflecting on your core values, your passions, and your strengths. And then asking, “How can I bring these to life in the world around me?”
The truth is, your ‘why’ is already there. It’s hidden in the moments when you feel most alive, most engaged, and truly fulfilled. These clues show up in your past—good times and tough times alike. If you think back, can you remember a moment when you felt genuinely proud, energized, or deeply satisfied? What were you doing? Who was with you? And what kind of impact did you have on others?
If you start to notice patterns in those memories, you’ll often find the underlying themes that point straight to your purpose.
So, how do you get started? Here are a few gentle steps you can try:
First, reflect on those formative experiences. Ask yourself, “When did I feel most alive? Where did I find meaning or joy that keeps showing up?”
Next, reach out to friends or colleagues you trust. Sometimes, they see strengths in us that we overlook ourselves. Their feedback can shine a light on what makes you, you.
And—don’t be afraid to experiment! Try new activities or roles that align with your values. Notice when you feel energized, or when something just clicks.
For instance, maybe you always find fulfillment in mentoring others. That could be your clue—your purpose might be about helping people grow and succeed. Or perhaps you’re at your best when you’re solving tough problems; your ‘why’ could be about creating order or sparking innovation.
Here’s something to keep in mind: your purpose isn’t set in stone. As you learn, grow, and encounter new opportunities, your ‘why’ can evolve right along with you. The key is to stay open, stay curious, and let your purpose guide the choices you make.
Once you have a sense of your ‘why’, think about ways to weave it into your daily life. Maybe that means seeking out projects or roles that match your values, volunteering for causes you care about, or simply bringing a fresh sense of meaning to your everyday routines.
Living with purpose isn’t about being perfect, or making big, dramatic gestures. It’s about the small, intentional choices you make—day after day—that reflect what truly matters to you. And over time, those choices add up, creating a life that feels deeply authentic, fulfilling, and connected to something bigger than yourself.
